clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old male presented with a nasal interpalpebral bulbar conjunctival mass in the right eye, characterized as firm, oval, dark brown, vascular, dome-shaped, non-mobile, and lobulated, measuring 7x6x3.2 mm. Initial examination and orbital MRI (E003) confirmed no intraocular extension. The patient underwent excisional biopsy with a no-touch technique, 3 mm margin, partial sclerectomy, and cryotherapy (E004). Intraoperatively, no intraocular extension was noted (E004). Histopathological examination of the excised mass revealed large vascular channels lined by endothelial cells and filled with red blood cells, separated by fibrous interstitium, with no signs of malignancy or necrosis (E005), confirming the diagnosis of conjunctival cavernous hemangioma. The patient showed no sign of recurrence after six months of follow-up (E007).
